threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for a napkin at food stalls, not realising everyone just uses their hands. And the seating is always first come, first served.
Caught a whiff of jerk chicken on the 333 last night; must’ve been a late-night vendor at the market. Smelled better than the usual boozy vibes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I heard a toddler shouting 'Bäcker!' at 8 AM and a neighbor responding with a perfectly timed, 'Ja, komm!'

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only here can you find spontaneous raves in abandoned buildings on a Tuesday night, complete with locals handing out homemade snacks.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local by their reaction to the BART delays—an eye roll and a knowing smirk, not panic. Tourists fumble with their phones, unsure what to do next.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a woman singing opera on the 31-Get off at the corner of Turk. Only in SF do people turn a bus ride into a concert.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the pretty squares, but they miss the real charm of the narrow streets where local cats sunbathe in the afternoons.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they still struggle to order in the cafés—getting the ‘café con leche’ and ‘cortado’ mixed up is a dead giveaway.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call them ‘scones’ and think the ‘cream tea’ debate will be civil. Just wait till you try ordering one at a cafe.
Last night on the 35, a guy serenaded the entire upper deck with Cher. We all clapped. Brixton nightlife never fails.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I saw a group of kids making a soccer field out of a pothole in the street, arguing fiercely over who would be the next Messi.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a club in a former factory that opens at dawn and serves breakfast raves—where techno meets scrambled eggs.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they order a burrito—with extra salsa, but never call it 'wet.' Those just visiting stick to the basics.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, I saw a guy giving an impromptu guitar lesson on the 14, while a toddler rode past on a scooter. Classic SF chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think parks here are just for lounging; locals know they’re the best places for neighborhood festivals and spontaneous concerts.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they stand at the tram stop, checking Google Maps every five minutes and looking up at the street signs like they’re in a foreign film.
